paper.title: Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks (Agent Skill Induction, ASI)
paper.central_claim: Web agents can adapt online by inducing, verifying by execution, and reusing program-based skills in their action space; on WebArena this beats a static agent and a text-skill adaptive agent (AWM) by 23.5% and 11.3% relative success rate, mainly through execution-based verification during induction, and reduces steps by 10.7-15.3%.

evidence.quote: But since ground-truth rewards are unavailable, an LLM-based evaluator
evidence.support_explanation: No ground-truth reward or demonstrations during the online stream; an LM evaluator V_L (claude-3.5-sonnet, same backbone) judges correctness (0/1) to select episodes for induction and again as check (1) of skill verification. Its error rate is not measured.

evidence.quote: If all three boxes are checked, we add the skills being called in the trajectory
evidence.support_explanation: Admission gate: (1) correctness of the re-executed trajectory by the LM evaluator, (2) at least one call to a new skill, (3) all skill-calling actions change the environment. Failed skills are simply not added; no repair loop, retirement or rollback.

evidence.quote: Next, to avoid spurious successes in skill verification, we truncate the trajectory yielded above by removing any trailing primitive actions after the last call to a skill program.
evidence.support_explanation: Concrete safeguard: trailing primitive actions (e.g. send_msg_to_user with the answer) are removed so a pass cannot come from the final primitive step alone.

evidence.quote: While a naive way is to query the agent with the same NL query and allow it to use newly induced skill actions, we find agents may not always use new skills due to the large search space of possible action trajectories.
evidence.support_explanation: Verification re-runs the same query with a rewritten skill-using prefix tau_D, so verification costs an extra environment rollout per attempted induction; the cost is not reported.

evidence.quote: This program-based evaluator enables relatively rigorous evaluation based on the functional correctness of the action trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Main metric is the official WebArena programmatic checker on 812 test examples across e-commerce, forum, GitLab, CMS and maps; a trustworthy outcome measure independent of the LM evaluator inside the loop.

evidence.quote: WebArena success rate by adaptive agents with programmatic skills, in comparison to a static vanilla agent baseline, and a text-skill learning adaptive agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Claude-3.5-Sonnet backbone: vanilla SR 32.7 / 5.6 steps, AWM 36.3 / 5.9, ASI 40.4 / 5.0 (absolute +7.7 and +4.1; the 23.5% and 11.3% are relative). Per site (ASI vs Claude vanilla / AWM): Shop 40.1 vs 32.6 / 34.8, Admin 44.0 vs 36.8 / 39.0, Reddit 54.7 vs 36.8 / 51.9, GitLab 32.2 vs 26.1 / 28.9, Maps 43.1 vs 38.5 / 39.4, Multi 20.8 vs 20.8 / 18.8 (tie with vanilla). The in-text step reductions are swapped relative to Table 1 (5.0 vs 5.6 is 10.7%, vs 5.9 is 15.3%). Single run, no variance, no significance test on this table.

evidence.quote: outperforms the static baseline agent and its text-skill counterpart by 23.5% and 11.3% in success rate, mainly thanks to the programmatic verification guarantee during the induction phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; the 'guarantee' rests on re-execution judged by the LM evaluator, which can pass wrong skills.

evidence.locator: Sec 3.3, Verified Induction Improves End Success Rate
evidence.quote: ), while always present skills in memory, improves end success rate by 4.2 points, indicating the importance of higher-quality induction via verification.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3 (shopping, n=180, one run): unverified text 32.6; verified program in memory 36.4; verified text in memory 39.0; verified program as actions (ASI) 40.1. The text's 4.2-point gain is 3.8 by the table, and 32.6 equals the vanilla shopping score, not AWM's 34.8 in Table 1.

signatures.object: Agent skill library A (callable Python programs in the web action space); baseline is the static primitive action space and AWM's text workflows in memory.
signatures.information: Episode (query, trajectory) for a WebArena task; LM evaluator verdict (no ground-truth reward, no demonstrations); accessibility-tree observations; induction is per website.
signatures.operation: Filter episodes by LM evaluator; clean steps and one-line thoughts; LM induces 1+ functions and rewrites the trajectory to call them; truncate trailing primitives; re-run the query with the rewritten prefix; add the called skills if correct, used and valid.
signatures.output: New callable skill actions in the action space.
signatures.conditions: Recurring procedures within a website; function size 2-5 steps; environment changes observable; LM evaluator reliability assumed.
signatures.feedback: Re-execution outcome judged by the LM evaluator plus usage and environment-change checks.
signatures.selection_rule: Admit only when correctness, skill usage and skill validity all hold (15.6% of attempted turns pass).
signatures.persistence: Skill library carried across episodes during the online stream; skills can be updated on a new site (+update) but no retirement or versioning is described.
signatures.later_use: Skills appear as actions in the policy's context and are called in later episodes (42.5% of examples reuse at least one).
signatures.claimed_effect: WebArena SR 40.4 vs 36.3 (AWM) vs 32.7 (vanilla); fewer steps; larger gains on long-horizon tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Skills tied to page constants or layouts become incompatible on new sites; LM judge may pass wrong skills; no repair loop; granularity and stability open.

signatures.object: Skill representation and usage channel: executable programs in the action space versus text in memory.
signatures.output: Shopping-site success rates isolating verification and format.
signatures.claimed_effect: Verification drives most of the gain; text suits memory, programs suit actuation.

gap.author_gap: Online adaptive web agents store induced knowledge as unverified text in memory (AWM), giving limited quality and no composition; offline demonstration collection is costly and mismatched.
gap.checked_gap: The fixed object (text skills in memory, admitted without checking) is specific, the nearest neighbour AWM is re-run under matched backbone and cleaning, and example analysis shows concrete defects. Other program-library work (LILO, TroVE-style, Voyager) is cited but not compared.
gap.lineage: Demonstrations-based and exploration-based skill learning -> online induction of workflows (AWM, text in memory) -> ASI: executable, verified, composable skills in the action space. Neighbours cited; AWM re-run in-paper; other neighbours not available as fixed local sources.
gap.closest_adjacent: AWM (Wang et al., 2024b); Voyager-style skill libraries, LILO/ReGAL-style program learning (cited only).
gap.residue: Skill granularity, stability of online evolution, quality versus human skills, and incompatibility under site changes.
gap.stakes: Efficiency and correctness on long-horizon web tasks; transfer to real sites.
gap.method_response: Represent skills as programs, verify by re-execution before admission, call them as actions.
gap.remaining_gap: Verification relies on an LM judge, no repair or retirement, single backbone, tiny transfer sets.
unresolved: Comparison with other program-library methods at equal cost could not be checked from fixed local sources.

rs_pattern.reason: Skills are emitted as executable programs (a machine-checkable intermediate artifact) and verified by re-execution before admission — decompose_and_delegate/C25. architectural_operator_substitution needs a cheaper surrogate with a proved preserved property; ASI offers no proof and its gain is not a cost substitution, so it is not kept (sol's own fit note says the guarantee condition fails).

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 2 machine-checkable intermediate artifact: executable skill programs, present. Step 3 close the loop with verifiable output applied during construction: re-execution with a skill-using prefix, present (judged partly by an LM evaluator). Step 4 ablate the verification step: present on one site (Table 3). Step 5 cost accounting: absent. Step 1 sound-solver boundary: the environment executes exactly but correctness is judged by an LM, so the solver is only partly sound.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: typed handoff artifact (function with args and docstring), closed feedback loop, growing reusable library. Failure: verification partly self-evaluated by the same LM, cost of delegation not reported, single benchmark family.
matches.reason: The load-bearing move is converting advisory text skills into executable objects whose use is verified by execution; C25 is chosen over adapt_via_conditioning (skills are not retrieved examples but actions) and over self_supervised_signal_engineering (the evaluator is a gate, not a training signal; no weights change).

rs_pattern.executes_pattern: partial (artifact + execution loop; verification bounded by an LM judge)
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: +4.1 SR over re-run AWM, single run

condition_checks: S1 admission gate is execution not judgment: partial (execution plus LM evaluator)
S2 admit only increments: partial (usage check, no re-derivability test)
S3 abstraction validated beyond source instance: partial (re-run on same query, reuse stats)
S4 repair driven by obtainable signals: unmet (no repair loop)
S5 retained library shown to carry the gain: partial (Table 3, vanilla comparison; no library-removed control)
H06-step1 practice source disjoint from evaluation: unmet (online stream is the test set)
matches.reason: H06 admission tactic (succeeded, invoked, changed environment) matches exactly; the practice source is the online test stream, not self-directed practice, hence medium.

revision_proposals: sol: online post-episode crystallisation is neither H06 practice nor H07 forging; consider a boundary note (proposal only).
Opus: evidence_gated_retention/H30 not assigned — ASI has admission only, no retirement; S2 is kept as a check question.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Executable program skills verified by re-execution (RS artifact-and-checker) correspond to H06's execution-gated admission into the action space; the growing validated library is the shared reuse capital.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: H06 needs a practice source disjoint from evaluation and a repair loop; ASI learns from the scored stream and has no repair. C25 needs a sound checker; here an LM evaluator is part of the check.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Skills induced online (no ground-truth reward) persist in the action space and are reused on later tasks (reuse 42.5% of the 725 tasks in Table 8); a fixed library also transfers to three real sites (10 queries each). Induction stream = scored stream.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Claude-3.5, single online pass on WebArena: ASI 40.4 vs re-run AWM 36.3 vs static 32.7 SR (relative +11.3%/+23.5%) with fewer macro-steps.
